id: Sunday Jazz Ft. The Cowie Quartet-The Undercurrent, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Sunday Jazz Ft. The Cowie Quartet
long_description:
This Sunday presents The Cowie Quartet! 

The Cowie Quartet invites you to The Undercurrent's first ever classical gig! 

Come along for a relaxed afternoon of varied string quartet music from across the globe. We'll be playing 19th-century classics by Borodin and Dvorak, jazz-inspired works of Takemitsu and Piazzolla, as well as unique folk song arrangements.

We are a newly formed quartet of students from the New Zealand School of Music, brought together by our goal to bring classical music out of the concert hall and into more venues around Wellington. Come hang out, have a drink, and enjoy some live classical music in a different kind of setting.

Sunday August 30
Doors 3pm
Music 3:30pm
$20 ($10 student)

Tickets available online and at the door!

As always, we are selling a range of refreshing drinks!

We still have our complimentary cheese crackers (we put the cheese on the crackers so you don’t have to do it) and tea and coffee, and of course...books available for purchase.

We hope to see you there! ⭐️

id: New Music Islands-Pyramid Club, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: New Music Islands
long_description:
Four Islands, Infinite Interpretations.

New Music Islands explores how we can forge connections across vast geographies while also doing our own thing, here, in our own way. The evening will be presented in two halves. The first 45 minutes feature a New Music Islands programme showcasing selected works from the Faroe Islands, Aotearoa New Zealand, the Canary Islands and Gotland. The second half celebrates the richness and diversity of contemporary music in New Zealand with a selection of works by New Zealand composers.

The programme centres on four works that embrace openness through flexible instrumentation and deliberately broad performance instructions. Each ensemble is invited to make the music their own, resulting in unique interpretations as the programme travels between the four island communities.

Featuring performances by Tristan Carter, Jonny Marks, Erika Grant, Naoto Segawa and Rebecca Steel, with music by Jesse Austin-Stewart, Ruby Solly, Elliot Vaughan, Ciro Hernández, Lasse Thornin, Weston Olencki, Michelle Scullion, Jessie Leov, Garling Wu and Chris Cree Brown.

Each concert will be a singular experience, with this being the Aotearoa New Zealand presentation. - New Music Islands is an international collaboration between four member societies of the International Society for Contemporary Music (ISCM): the Faroe Islands Section, VICC (ISCM Gotland Section), COSIMITE (ISCM Affiliated Associate Member representing the Canary Islands) and CANZ (ISCM New Zealand Section).

name: Katelyn Henshall EP Release With Jeline And Ari Leason
long_description:
Katelyn Henshall fuses pop, R&B, and soul into something uniquely her own. Fronting the genre of what she claims to be whiskey lounge soul, Katelyn and her band are excited to share live performances from their debut EP, A lil somethin' somethin'. Kicking off 2026 with a bang, Katelyn has released two singles, Take Me Away and Nothing lasts forever (de verano), in anticipation of the full EP. A lil somethin’ somethin’” is a tasting tray of a few of the genres Katelyn is passionate about, showcasing the strengths and skills of every member of the band. Katelyn's band consists of Dónal Gunning (bass), Tane James (guitar), and Oliver Dudziak (drums).

Ōtaki-born singer-songwriter Ari Leason will open the show. Her soulful blend of indie folk and intimate storytelling shines through her debut album Hello Darling. Honest, vulnerable, and deeply authentic, Ari brings songs shaped by activism, travel, and a coming-of-age journey that resonates long after the last note.

Also supporting Katelyn is jeline, your ‘filipina-next door’ - an indie-pop-rock artist who's writing songs about feelings she can't contain to herself and belting her heart out to whoever's listening! jeline has surrounded herself in different genres and music tastes but after trying to find her feet as an artist, some honest talks with the industry and scrapping a whole ass album, she finally locked in to her recognisable indie-pop-rock sound. From songs about first love to obsessing over exes, jeline's relatability and vulnerability is always packaged in a song you can bop along to.

Venue accessibility information:

Vogelmorn Upstairs is not a wheelchair accessible building. There is an accessible
bathroom in the space. This is an all ages venue but those under the age of 16 must be
accompanied by a designated adult after 8pm. The Vogelmorn Precinct is a community
space located in a residential area. With that in mind, the team ask that you be kind to
others' and that when you leave the gig, you do so quietly to avoid disturbing our
neighbours.

Come early before the show and enjoy a meal at Vogelmorn's restaurant, VBC Eats, from 4:00pm to 9:00pm. VBC Eats is a relaxed community-focused restaurant delivering tasty specials, from curries to salads to pizzas to bite-sized bar snacks. By locals for locals!

name: DEATHRO (Japan)
long_description:
DEATHRO (Japan) returns to Te Whanganui-a-Tara!

Friday 4 September, Chain Punk Baddie and Swamp Soul present a special show at the Newtown Bowls Club, together with a stacked lineup of sick bands from all over - Unsanitary Napkin (Te Whanganui-a-Tara/Ōtepoti), Crook (Tāmaki Makaurau), Forced Starvation (Te Whanganui-a-Tara), Silicon Tongue (Te Whanganui-a-Tara), and Western Haikus (Te Whanganui-a-Tara).

-------------

Kanagawa Japan’s #1 rock vocalist DEATHRO returns to Aotearoa in September 2026, presented by Wrought Material and Chain Punk Baddie. Beloved by the Tokyo punk underground, DEATHRO combines new wave, post-punk, and J-Rock into high-energy BEATROCK in the 1980’s Japanese tradition.

DEATHRO’s performance is ecstatic and powerful, while the lyrics are grounded in working class politics. DEATHRO has a punk mind and expresses it. Amongst messages of solidarity, freedom of expression, and love for his hometown Kanagawa, DEATHRO tackles the injustice of colonisation and the oppression of the Palestinian people.

DEATHRO will be joined by UNSANITARY NAPKIN from Te Whanganui-a-Tara/Ōtepoti for all shows, and supported by local legends in each centre.

DEATHRO showcases his high energy beatrock performances in an extensive journey across both Te Ika-a-Māui and Te Waipounamu this September, including a stop at Great Sounds Great Festival in Te Whanganui-a-Tara. Don't miss it!

long_description:
The Undercurrent presents a Film Screening of Mauri!

Join us for a free community screening of Mauri, directed by Maurizio and Zaya Benazzo and part of The Eternal Song, an extraordinary 13-film documentary journey exploring Indigenous wisdom, ancestral knowledge, resilience and healing across cultures.

Filmed in Aotearoa, Mauri journeys alongside Māori healers, elders and knowledge keepers, exploring colonisation, intergenerational trauma, identity, whenua and pathways of healing.

We'll gather first over kai and conversation, then share a gentle 15-minute grounding, gratitude and connection practice before immersing ourselves together in this powerful 70-minute film.

Start 6pm
Free entry

Snacks, a range of refreshing drinks, tea & coffee, and of course...books available for purchase!

id: Mel Parsons - Castle Hill Album Release Tour-The Opera House, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Mel Parsons - Castle Hill Album Release Tour
long_description:
Singer-songwriting luminary, Mel Parsons, has announced a seven-date national theatre tour with her band in August and September 2026, celebrating her much-anticipated new album, CASTLE HILL, to released on August 7.

Plus1 proudly presents Mel Parsons live around Aotearoa in some of our country's most beautiful theatres.

Thursday August 27 - Theatre Royal, Nelson
Friday August 28 - Isaac Theatre Royal, Christchurch
Saturday August 29 - Glenroy Auditorium, Dunedin
Thursday September 3 - Clarence St Theatre, Hamilton
Friday September 4 - Q Theatre, Rangatira - Auckland
Saturday September 5 - Opera House, Wellington
Sunday September 6 - Globe Theatre, Palmerston North

Full tour info at plus1.co.nz and MelParsons.com

Taking its name from the remote mountain town in the Southern Alps where it was recorded, CASTLE HILL was produced by Josh Logan and recorded live with Mel’s longtime band members Aaron Stewart (bass) and Jed Parsons (drums); joined by Ben King (Goldenhorse, Grand Rapids) on guitars. Parsons says of these sessions: “it was a full immersion recording experience over a stolen summer holiday”

Following the release of SABOTAGE in 2024, multi-award winning Parsons toured the country with Crowded House, performed in Canada and Australia, and has continued her stellar run including a finalist nod for Best Folk Artist at the 2026 AMA’s.

Singles already released from the record include the alternative radio chart toppers Post High Slide, Brick By Brick, Be Here Now, Don't Leave The Light On, and Caravan, as well as new single Grain By Grain. Castle Hill album release tour is funded through NZ On Air and supported by the NZ Music Commission.

Expect soaring harmonies, a dynamic live show, and a feel-good vibe throughout as Mel Parsons performs live this August and September. Come and celebrate one of Aotearoa’s finest live artists!

name: Great Sounds Great Festival 2026
venue: Multiple venues across the Cuba Street precinct, Wellington
long_description:
Eyegum Music Collective presents GREAT SOUNDS GREAT, a multi-venue music and arts festival taking over Pōneke's Te Aro precinct for one night only on Saturday 5 September 2026. Showcasing 40 of Aotearoa's best artists across 10 neighbouring venues, this is one big party you shouldn't miss.

Eyegum has worked hard to curate a programme that is sure to offer something for everyone, from first time gig-goers to seasoned live music obsessives. The eclectic lineup includes national treasures like Bic Runga and Savage, heavy-hitting legends Beastwars, Kody Nielson’s enigmatic project Silicon, indie math rockers So So Modern, powerhouse party starter Mokotron, local hip hop sensation MĀ, and everything in between.

Tonic Collective are back with an impeccably curated lineup for their travelling stage, which includes Pitch Black celebrating 30 years as Aotearoa electronica pioneers and award winning sonic explorer Amamelia.

It's not all music, three of our best poets Chris Tse, Dani Yourukova, and Jackson McCarthy will also perform.

Excitingly for 2026, we are adding a new venue, the incomparable Meow Nui, helping make this year's event bigger and better than ever. We are also throwing a warm-up party, The Night Before, across three venues in Newtown village on Friday 4 September. This will showcase 12 incredible up-and-coming artists and is the perfect way to prepare for the main event.

Ticket holders will receive a wristband that will give them access to each of the participating venues throughout the event. Information on how to pick up wristbands will be provided to ticket holders closer to the time.

Limited tickets on sale now from eyegum.co.nz/great-sounds-great

Presented with support from Abandoned Brewery, RadioActive.FM, and Wellington City Council.

Venues: Meow Nui, San Fran, Meow, Valhalla, Rogue & Vagabond, Bedlam & Squalor, Hotel Bristol, St Peter's on Willis, Flying Nun Records, Tonic Travelling Stage.

Eyegum Music Collective presents GREAT SOUNDS GREAT, a multi-venue music and arts festival taking over Pōneke's Te Aro precinct for one night only on Saturday 5 September 2026.
Tonic Collective are back with an impeccably curated lineup for their travelling stage, which includes Pitch Black celebrating 30 years as Aotearoa electronica pioneers and award winning sonic explorer Amamelia.
This will showcase 12 incredible up-and-coming artists and is the perfect way to prepare for the main event.
Information on how to pick up wristbands will be provided to ticket holders closer to the time.
Lineup: Amamelia, Beastwars, Bic Runga, Bri Louise, Chris Tse, Crook, Cruelly, Dani Yourukova, Deathro (JPN), Dream Chambers, Fazed on a Pony, Groove Council, Hemi Hemingway, Hihi & The Stitchbirds, Hunter Jackson, In Good Company, Jackson McCarthy, JELL, Ludus b2b Rizzo, MĀ, Mauri Aura, mHz, Mokotron, More Blue Noise, Naakz & Babyzoot, Office Dog, Pearly*, Pitch Black, Savage (DJ Set), Savagehine, Sheeps, Silicon, So So Modern, Soft Bait, Tamatha Paul, The Sour, The Spectre Collective: Live-Scored Cinema, Tūi Band, Unsanitary Napkin.
